title: Choir and Veil
premise: Theo Reyes, a bone-carver who hears the voices of the dead through the relics he carves, has spent years avoiding the war creeping toward the free cities. When a mute child arrives at his door speaking a language older than any kingdom, Theo learns she is the last vessel of the true king's memory — and that the thing wearing the crown is a veil-born parasite that devours its host slowly, feeding on a nation's grief. Guided by smuggler roads and the dead who remember every betrayal, Theo must carry the child to the ruined choir beneath Thornfell where the usurper was first bound, unbind the dying king from his parasite, and choose between the justice of law and the mercy of memory. In the end Theo gives up his own gift to silence the veil forever, the child speaks her first word in the common tongue, and the free cities stand — but Theo no longer hears the dead, only the living.
about_author: Bram Almeida is the pen name of a former stonemason turned novelist who writes fantasy rooted in labor, craft, and the quiet violence of borders. They live in a coastal town where they carve bone chess pieces and claim, only half-jokingly, to take plot advice from the sea.

chapters.title: The Knucklebone Winter
chapters.summary: POV Theo. In the mountain town of Greyhollow, Theo carves a dead woman's knucklebone into a keepsake and endures her ghost's final words: 'the crown lies.' Establishes his gift as both livelihood and curse, his debts to smugglers, and his careful neutrality as war rumors reach the passes. Emotional beat: weary isolation.

chapters.title: A Child at the Door
chapters.summary: POV Theo. During a whiteout storm, a girl of eight appears at Theo's workshop, barefoot and unharmed by cold, speaking a language that makes his carved bones resonate like struck bells. She carries a locket of royal seal-bone. The dead in his workshop go silent for the first time in his life. Emotional beat: dread wrapped in wonder.

chapters.title: What the Dead Refuse to Say
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo interrogates his ghosts about the child; all flee or fall silent except one — a hanged smuggler who whispers the name Veilborn before dissolving. A bounty notice arrives naming the girl as a runaway asset of the crown. Theo must decide whether to sell her out or run. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility hardening into choice.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo calls in an old debt with Sefa Marun, a one-eyed caravan mistress who knows every blind path through Thornfell. She agrees to move them south — but warns that the passes are being sealed by the usurper's Graycloaks. First glimpse of the wider war through refugee traffic. Emotional beat: fragile alliance.

chapters.title: Voices in the Bone Road
chapters.summary: POV the child, Ilset. Through her eyes we learn she is not fully human: she is a vessel grown from the true king's severed memories, fleeing the palace when the Veil began eating the king's mind. Her POV renders the world strange and luminous. Emotional beat: terror of being hunted for what you contain.

chapters.title: Graycloak Checkpoint
chapters.summary: POV Theo. At the Salt Stair pass, a Graycloak captain inspects the caravan and nearly finds Ilset; Theo bluffs using a forged relic, but the captain recognizes him from an old warrant. They escape over a cliff path with a death behind them and a name on a list ahead. Emotional beat: adrenaline curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: The Chapel of Unfinished Kings
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Sheltering in a ruined chapel, Ilset dreams aloud and Theo witnesses the coronation of King Aldric — and the moment the Veil entered the crown, a bargain made to end a plague. The dead king's voice reaches Theo directly for the first time: 'I asked for this. I was wrong.' Emotional beat: pity for an enemy-king.

chapters.title: Sefa's Price
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Flashback chapter: twenty years ago Sefa smuggled for Aldric's court and lost her eye and her brother to the crown's secret police. She reveals she isn't helping Theo out of friendship — she wants the Veil exposed so her brother's execution can be named murder, not treason. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Turn Their Faces
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Reaching the free city of Vessany, Theo seeks scholars who can read Ilset's language; instead he finds councils voting to negotiate with the usurper rather than fight. A scholar confirms the Veil cannot be killed, only unbound — and only at the choir where it was first sung into the crown. Emotional beat: despair at institutional cowardice.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bone Market
chapters.summary: POV Theo. A Vessany fence sells Theo's location to the Graycloaks. In a running fight through the market, Theo uses the dead — animating relic-bones into a shield of ancestors — revealing his gift publicly and making himself a target alongside Ilset. Sefa extracts them by river. Emotional beat: the cost of being seen.

chapters.title: Ilset Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Ilset. Under strain, Ilset begins leaking the king's memories into waking life, calling Theo by a courtier's name and weeping for a queen Theo never knew existed. She confesses she was made to be consumed — a spare vessel if the Veil outgrew the king. Emotional beat: heartbreak and fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Mercy
chapters.summary: POV antagonist interlude — the Veil wearing King Aldric. It is not cruel; it genuinely believes it is saving the kingdom from the plague of memory, erasing grief one village at a time. It orders the army toward Thornfell not from malice but from a terrible, patient love. Emotional beat: chilling sympathy for the monster.

chapters.title: Ash Over Thornfell
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The party climbs into the high passes as the usurper's vanguard burns the foothills. Theo's ghosts grow louder near the old choir site — thousands of dead packed into the stone like sediment. Sefa is wounded holding a rearguard action. Emotional beat: mounting dread, love confessed in crisis.

chapters.title: The Choir Beneath
chapters.summary: POV Theo. They descend into the sunken cathedral where the Veil was first bound: a cavern of resonant stone where the dead still sing the binding-song on loop. Theo learns the unbinding requires a living voice fluent in the old tongue — which means Ilset must sing it, and singing will empty her. Emotional beat: horror at the price.

chapters.title: Sefa's Verdict
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Wounded and dying, Sefa argues against sacrificing the child: justice outside the law means refusing lawful arithmetic that spends children to save kingdoms. She gives Theo her ledger of the crown's crimes as evidence to speak at the unbinding. Emotional beat: moral clarity purchased with blood.

chapters.title: The Graycloaks Descend
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The vanguard reaches the mountain; Theo collapses the pass with carved charge-bones and the help of the avalanche-dead, buying hours. Ilset, having overheard everything, quietly prepares to sing anyway. Theo realizes he can't stop her — only stand beside her. Emotional beat: surrender to shared sacrifice.

chapters.title: Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The Veil arrives early, alone, leaving its army at the pass — curious about the vessel that fled. In the choir it offers Theo a bargain: restore his dead mother's voice in exchange for Ilset. Theo refuses, and the refusal breaks something open in the king buried beneath. Emotional beat: temptation resisted.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV alternating Theo/Ilset. Ilset sings the binding-song reversed while Theo carves the king's memories into new bone, giving the dying Aldric a body of witness. The Veil, unbound from crown and host, unravels into the choir of the dead — who finally stop singing and let it rest. Aldric dies human, forgiven. Emotional beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: What Silence Costs
chapters.summary: POV Theo. The gift leaves Theo as the choir goes quiet — the dead released, his workshop-minds gone. He grieves the loss of a sense more than a skill, mourning the mother-voice he never heard again. Ilset wakes speaking common tongue, ordinary and alive. Emotional beat: hollowed-out peace.

chapters.title: Evidence Before the Councils
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Theo presents Sefa's ledger and Aldric's testimony-bones to the free cities' council, forcing justice outside their negotiated peace: the crown's crimes named, the dead smugglers pardoned posthumously. Some accept; some don't. The war dissolves without a battle fought. Emotional beat: imperfect, earned vindication.

chapters.title: The Carver's Hands
chapters.summary: POV Theo. Months later, Theo returns to Greyhollow and carves again — plain work now, no voices, just craft. He takes Ilset as an apprentice, teaching her to shape bone without hearing what it remembers. Sefa's ledger becomes a public archive bearing her name. Emotional beat: quiet rebuilding.

chapters.title: One Word
chapters.summary: POV Ilset. On the anniversary of the unbinding, Ilset finishes her first solo carving — a small bird — and gives it to Theo with a single word of the old tongue, the one word of the dead that stayed with her: it means 'stay.' Theo stays. The book closes on the two of them in the workshop, alive, listening to nothing but each other. Emotional beat: tender resolution.
